title: Dorian Ashwood
dek: A caravan musician whose friendship, grief and care repeatedly confront him with the difference between protecting someone and forcing an answer.

facts.Recorded at: The Gate and road to Pristinia

Selected primary scenes and established public histories; anchors below
body:
Through the wrong curtain

Dorian says he was about to perform with his family’s travelling caravan when he passed through a curtain and found himself in the forest. He introduces himself as Dorian Ashwood and carries a guitar. He also says that, unlike his family, he has been unable to use magic despite practice.

Safety in people

Vaemyr raises his hands to reassure him, warns that the Gate has recently been attacked, and leads him toward Pristinia. His explanation of the war and his warnings about dangerous magic remain a guide’s account of the world.

More than a fighter

Dorian promises to help as best he can. Vaemyr urges steady growth and asking for help, then tells him he does not have to fight: there are many ways to serve a good cause. The encounter records a commitment to contribute, not a completed career or allegiance.

Music before the crisis

Dorian’s history includes ordinary pleasure as well as violence. In August 2024 he plays guitar with a friend accompanying him on violin in the square. The scene names him Dorian Ashwood and preserves the companionship that gives his later grief context.

Swift-Foot · grief seeks certainty

When he sees Swift’s head, his response is anger held with difficulty. His affection for Swift makes the witnesses’ account painful to accept. The death investigation does not become simple merely because he wants a different answer.

Dorian asks Vaemyr to accompany him while he questions the witnesses and warns him to bear with a method learned from an old master. Lucido worries that he will cause harm; Vaemyr says he is telling Dorian not to hurt the men. The preserved account of their confrontation describes Vaemyr standing between his friend and torture. It does not justify recording an injury that the reviewed main-channel sequence does not show.

Friendship here includes opposition. Vaemyr’s restraint protects the witnesses while resisting a course that could consume Dorian’s grief. It does not prove the Rahu testimony complete or settle every question about Swift’s intentions.

Leo and the work after violence

In the later cave confrontation, Dorian argues with Arjahn and describes tying and carrying Leo out. His post also conditionally proposes taking the crystal if it remains intact; the narrator asks him to choose. The account does not turn that conditional declaration into two completed actions or independently settle Leo’s condition.

His next training scenes show attempts to save patients and satisfaction at having helped someone survive. They also contain threats and anger. Those conflicting choices belong to the same person: care is visible, but does not erase the harm he threatens.

The open record

The extent of his actions in the witness side-room, Leo’s precise condition during the proposed carrying and Dorian’s later response to Swift’s death still require fuller reconstruction. His earlier musical life and practical care remain part of his history rather than being displaced by one moral crisis.

Recorded scenes

Dates refer to transcript postings, not an independently established in-world calendar.

  • 7 August · Swift’s head

  • Lucido’s concern
